baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired causatives in 'أماته فأقبره', ordered by ثم and then ف, attach both death and emplacement to the same acting subject.
baseline_models.mechanism: Vital force is first removed and the resulting dead person is then given burial. The second act is not swallowed by the first: death creates an exposed, dependent body, and emplacement answers that new condition.

activation_trace.role: Causative removal of force supplies the first transition and makes the subject unable to manage what follows.
Burial or provision of a grave supplies the answering placement of the now-dependent dead person.

changed_reading.before: Then he died and was buried, as two facts in a biography.
changed_reading.after: Then He actively ended the person's vitality and, as a distinct answering act, secured a grave for the body.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence joins causative death at word 2 to causative grave-placement at word 3.
baseline_models.mechanism: The line performs a two-stage reduction: animation is stilled, then visibility and elevation are reduced by enclosure below the surface. The temporal syntax turns these into successive transformations of the same human subject.

activation_trace.role: Stillness and lifeless inactivity render the first verb as deactivation rather than mere calendar expiry.
A hidden, sunken, or enclosed state supplies the spatial second stage after bodily stilling.

changed_reading.before: Death is followed by the conventional location called a grave.
changed_reading.after: The human is first deactivated and then deliberately transferred out of the visible surface into a lowered, enclosed state.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The form 'أقبره' can activate not only burial but the giving or permitting of a grave.
baseline_models.mechanism: Once life and strength are gone, the dead body cannot protect its own exposure. Grave-provision functions as a final material allowance: the person is not merely discarded but granted a bounded resting place.

activation_trace.role: Loss of life and strength establishes the body's complete dependence after death.
Providing or permitting a grave turns burial into a bestowed protection and place, not only disposal.

changed_reading.before: Burial is a neutral postmortem procedure.
changed_reading.after: Burial is a provision made for a powerless body, preserving bounded place and dignity after vitality has left.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening attention drama makes the two divine causatives read as a counter-pattern: a striving person can be turned away from and neglected by a human, whereas the powerless dead person is not left unattended but is brought through death into a provided grave.

activation_trace.role: Provision of burial anchors the changed reading in a concrete act of attending to the dead.
Turning away supplies the negative social motion against which grave-provision becomes conspicuous non-abandonment.
Purposeful movement toward a sought end marks the living petitioner's effort that nevertheless meets diverted attention.
Being occupied away from someone sharpens the contrast with the unskipped care encoded by the second causative.

structural_cues: The opening sequence opposes an arriving, striving person to human turning-away and diversion; 80:21 again gives a person two successive treatments by an agent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposed motions of approach, withdrawal, and diversion plus later grave-provision; I supply the contrast between human selective attention and divine completion of care. The live alternative is that the episodes are sequential but not contrastive.

changed_reading.before: The grave is simply what happens after death.
changed_reading.after: The grave is also an act of non-abandonment: even when the human can no longer approach, ask, or strive, the sequence does not turn away from the body.

context_deltas.mechanism: Written sheets, custodial hands, and a book that discloses what is written activate an archival analogy for the grave. The body is enclosed and deposited rather than erased, held through an interval before a later disclosure.

activation_trace.role: Hidden, lowered enclosure gives the grave the material shape of a sealed repository.
The written sheet supplies the archive domain: material can be deposited while its content remains recoverable.
Handing and conveyance supply custodial transfer as the functional analogy for emplacement.
A book that uncovers writing makes concealment compatible with later disclosure rather than destruction.

structural_cues: The honored, elevated, purified sheets in custodial hands precede the compact human life-cycle sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies protected written matter, hands of conveyance, disclosure, and a hidden enclosure; I supply the cross-domain mapping of corpse to deposited record and grave to archive. A live alternative is that the written-material sequence bears no spatial relation to burial.

changed_reading.before: The grave hides remains because they are finished with.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the grave stores the embodied human as a protected deposit: hidden for an interval, not erased from eventual disclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby condemnation joins violent death-language to the human act of covering. That activates an asymmetry in 80:21: the human culpably covers truth or gift, yet after death is himself mercifully covered and placed out of exposure.

activation_trace.role: Caused death anchors the physical transition that answers the nearby death-directed imprecation.
Burial supplies a protective physical covering and allotted place for the very human under condemnation.
Taking life supplies an intensified lexical neighbor to the focus act of causing death.
Covering and concealment supply the moral action that is materially reversed into merciful covering of the corpse.

structural_cues: The condemnation of the human immediately opens the creation-to-death sequence, so the condemned coverer and the buried human are grammatically continuous.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies death, culpable covering, and burial; I distinguish the direction I add: the burial-cover is protective, unlike the human's blameworthy covering. The alternative is a root-image echo without an intended ethical reversal.

changed_reading.before: Burial is morally unmarked concealment after death.
changed_reading.after: Burial becomes a strikingly protective cover granted to the human whose own covering is condemned, holding severity and care together.

context_deltas.mechanism: Creation is measured, the route is extended, and movement through it is eased before vitality is removed and a grave supplied. The focus pair therefore belongs to the same administered trajectory as formation and passage, rather than entering as an unmanaged accident.

activation_trace.role: Causative loss of force supplies the designed route's terminal deactivation.
Provision of a grave supplies a destination after the enabled path, not an accidental leftover.
Measuring and proportioning make bodily formation an administered first phase.
Deliberative ordering supplies the planning frame that can extend through death and placement.
An extended traversable road turns life into movement along a supplied course.
Opening and ease after difficulty make the preceding route actively enabled by the same agency.

structural_cues: Repeated third-person causatives share one object pronoun across creating, measuring, easing, causing death, and providing burial.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a tightly repeated agent-object grammar and branch images of design, road, ease, death, and grave; I infer one administered trajectory across them. The alternative is a list of powers without a functional route model.

changed_reading.before: Death interrupts a life whose designed phases have already ended.
changed_reading.after: Death and grave-placement are themselves administered phases of the measured route, with the grave functioning as its next assigned station.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next divine action opens, spreads, and revives the dead when willed. Read backward, the grave's hidden enclosure is a bounded holding state between two opposed causatives: vitality is removed and the person is enclosed, then the enclosure is reversed by renewed animation and expansion.

activation_trace.role: Loss of vitality defines the state that the following revival reverses.
Hidden and sunken enclosure becomes the compressed middle state that can later be opened.
Will attached to the act prevents the transition out of burial from being automatic or self-generated.
Opening, spreading, and branching supply a spatial reversal of the grave's compressed concealment.
Reviving the dead supplies the direct vital reversal of the preceding causative death.

structural_cues: Three successive verses use ثم and the same object pronoun for death, grave-placement, and later raising.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet explicitly supplies death followed by grave and willed revival; I infer that the grave functions as reversible containment rather than merely lying between events. The alternative is that resurrection follows burial without the grave itself carrying a holding function.

changed_reading.before: The grave is the terminal result of death.
changed_reading.after: The grave is a deliberately closed middle chamber in a reversible sequence: deanimation and contraction await willed reanimation and opening.

context_deltas.mechanism: The declaration that the human has not completed what was commanded changes the force of caused death. Biological agency is closed and the body emplaced while commanded agency remains incomplete; burial terminates capacity without settling the account.

activation_trace.role: Removal of strength closes the person's remaining capacity to act.
Burial materially closes the person's worldly field while leaving the issue of performance unresolved.
Completion and bringing an undertaking to its end supply the standard the human has not reached.
Binding demand supplies the unfinished obligation that outlasts the person's ability to perform.

structural_cues: The negated completion statement follows immediately after death, burial, and raising, refusing to let the life-cycle sequence imply successful fulfillment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies bodily closure and explicitly uncompleted command; I infer that death ends capacity but not accountability. The alternative is that 80:23 evaluates humanity generally without focusing the grave as the point of interrupted agency.

changed_reading.before: Burial closes a completed human life.
changed_reading.after: Burial can close the body's agency while its commanded work remains unfinished, making the grave a boundary of capacity rather than a discharge of obligation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later earth sequence activates a seed model: something lifeless is hidden below the surface; the earth is split; growth and grain emerge. The grave can therefore be carried as latency in earth, not only disposal into earth, while the prior resurrection statement keeps the analogy from becoming autonomous naturalism.

activation_trace.role: Lifeless land and inert matter bridge bodily death to a material state that can await renewed productivity.
Lowered concealment supplies the beneath-the-surface placement shared by grave and seed.
The earth's splitting and opening supply the outward motion that can reverse grave closure.
Soft productive earth changes the burial medium from inert cover into a site capable of emergence.
Vegetation coming out of earth supplies the emergence phase of the latent-body analogy.
A seed that sprouts and bears grain supplies the compact hidden carrier from which multiplicative life appears.

structural_cues: The same passage moves from human interment and raising to repeated first-person causatives that open earth and bring growth out of it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies dead matter, lowered concealment, opening earth, growth, and seed; I supply the corpse-to-seed mapping and the arrow from burial to latency. The alternative is that the food cycle demonstrates provision without modeling the grave.

changed_reading.before: The grave is earth used to hide a finished body.
changed_reading.after: The grave can coexistently read as seed-like latency: the body is placed beneath a surface whose packet-images already carry splitting, emergence, and renewed life.

context_deltas.mechanism: Burial is normally performed by others, yet the grave encloses one body. The later flight from brother, companion, and children, with each person wholly occupied by an individual affair, activates the grave as the first material grammar of singularization: communal handling yields to irreducibly individual placement and standing.

activation_trace.role: A grave as the dead person's resting place anchors singular emplacement even when burial is socially performed.
Flight supplies active severance from the relations that ordinarily accompany and bury a person.
Brotherhood and kinship supply one of the strongest bonds shown as unable to absorb another's standing.
Close companionship supplies habitual co-presence that is later broken into separate trajectories.
Filial descent and relation to an origin supply continuity that cannot prevent individual separation.
Totality and enclosure make each person's absorption complete rather than partial.
An individual affair or grave concern supplies what occupies each person beyond relational transfer.

structural_cues: The branchless ص خ خ cue at 80:33 is used only structurally as the abrupt threshold before the ordered list of fleeing kin.
The kin list expands from brother through parents to companion and children, then collapses into 'each person' and 'an affair'.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies one-person grave emplacement, kinship, flight, and total individual preoccupation; I infer burial as an anticipatory material form of singular accountability. The alternative is that funeral community and eschatological flight remain unrelated scenes.

changed_reading.before: Burial is the community's final act upon one of its members.
changed_reading.after: Burial is also the first hard boundary of singular standing: others may place the body, but neither grave nor later affair can be inhabited by kin on the person's behalf.

context_deltas.mechanism: The grave hides and lowers the body; the final scene reverses that privacy into exposed, readable faces. Uncovering and radiance mark one set, while earth-colored dust, overpowering accretion, and facial darkening mark another. Burial's concealment is temporary because the person returns as a publicly legible surface.

activation_trace.role: Hidden and sunken emplacement supplies the private, unreadable middle state that the face scene reverses.
The face as the forward visible surface supplies the site on which the formerly hidden person becomes public.
Removing a cover supplies the direct spatial reversal of grave concealment.
Dust and earth-color transfer the burial medium onto the now-visible face as a readable mark.
Overpowering coverage supplies an active accretion on the face, unlike the neutral enclosure of the grave.
Facial darkening makes the returned person's condition visibly legible rather than subterraneously hidden.

structural_cues: The closing contrast is organized by repeated 'faces that day', turning persons into exposed surfaces after the burial interval.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies grave-concealment followed by uncovered or dust-covered faces; I infer a concealment-to-legibility reversal and a transfer of earth from surrounding medium to facial sign. The alternative is simple temporal succession without material transfer.

changed_reading.before: Burial removes the body from view once and for all.
changed_reading.after: Burial is temporary unreadability: the hidden person later returns as a face whose condition is exposed, differentiated, and impossible to outsource.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because submission is a form-distant branch of موت and the grave keeps literal death primary. It remains anchored in 'أماته' and gains contextual pressure from awe and uncompleted command. Downstream prose should present it only as a secondary resonance of forced yielding at life's end, never as a replacement translation for physical death.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The causative موت form can carry a remote resonance of making the person yield, immediately followed by lowering and concealment in the grave.

activation_trace.role: Submission to truth supplies a secondary yielding resonance within the causative death verb.
Lowered concealment gives the possible yielding a concrete terminal bodily realization.
Fear joined with awe supplies the earlier possibility of voluntary receptive yielding.
Binding command supplies the truth-claim before which terminal yielding occurs despite unfinished performance.

changed_reading.before: He ended the person's biological life and buried him.
changed_reading.after: Alongside literal death, the line may faintly resonate as the point where resistance is made to yield and the person is physically lowered before the truth left unfulfilled.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is deliberately branch-distant: the nose-tip raised in anger is not the contextual meaning of 'أقبره'. It remains worth carrying because the odd focus branch is anchored to ق ب ر and the surah frames the sequence with a contracted face and later exposed faces. Render only as a motif-level resonance in which grave-lowering contains visible hauteur, never as lexical substitution.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: A remote ق ب ر branch at word 3 concerns the raised nose-tip in anger, while the actual construction still denotes grave-placement.

activation_trace.role: The anger-marked nose-tip supplies a remote image of elevated facial self-display that grave-lowering can contain.
Facial contraction from distress or anger establishes visible face-management at the passage's opening.
The forward visible face reopens the motif after the hidden interval of burial.

changed_reading.before: Grave-placement concerns only the body's location.
changed_reading.after: As a contained secondary echo, lowering into the grave also levels the raised, managed face that organizes social aversion, anger, and status.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading is surprising because heart-deadness is not asserted of the person in 80:21, and literal causative death plus burial controls the line. It remains anchored through a live موت branch activated by blindness of insight and covering truth. Downstream prose should qualify it as a possible inner-to-outer resonance, not a claim that God first caused moral unbelief.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus موت inventory at word 2 includes deadness of heart, while the following grave gives deadness an overt bodily endpoint.

activation_trace.role: Deadness of heart supplies an inner loss of perception that can echo within the literal caused death.
Bodily concealment and lowering make an otherwise inward deadness materially visible as a terminal state.
Blindness of heart and insight activates a non-ocular perceptual failure without assigning it to the physically blind visitor.
Concealing truth supplies the active epistemic counterpart to inner deadness.
Reviving the dead keeps even the completed bodily state within a larger possibility of reversal.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports only the end and concealment of bodily life.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, bodily death and burial can externalize an earlier possibility of inward non-perception, while the next act retains divine capacity to reverse deadness.

strongest_changes: The immediate willed raising revises the grave from endpoint into reversible containment between deanimation and reopening.
The uncompleted command makes burial a boundary of human capacity without making it a discharge of accountability.
The split-earth and seed sequence activates burial as latency in productive earth rather than disposal into inert earth.
The final exposed faces reverse the grave's hidden body into a publicly legible and individually differentiated person.
The condemned human's moral covering coexists with protective bodily covering, so severity and grave-provision remain in tension.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah is unusually compressed: two same-agent causatives turn one person from vitality to dependence and then from exposure to bounded concealment. The grave's hidden/sunken branch became a hub that could coexistently behave as provision, archive, temporary chamber, seed-bed, individual boundary, and the negative of later exposed faces.
remaining_uncertainties: How much force to assign specifically to providing a grave versus directly causing burial in the form 'أقبره'.
Whether the archive and seed mechanisms are intended cross-domain links or reader-activated analogies from sequence and branch imagery.
Whether submission and heart-deadness should survive beyond contained secondary resonance, since literal death and burial remain controlling.
Whether later face and kin scenes actively reinterpret the grave or only become compatible retrospective models.
